superslicer.bridge_type.label: Bridge flow baseline
superslicer.bridge_type.tooltip:
This setting allow you to choose the base for the bridge flow compute, the result will be multiplied by the bridge flow to have the final result.
A bridge is an infill extrusion with nothing under it to flatten it, and so it can't have a 'rectangle' shape but a circle one.
 * The default way to compute a bridge flow is to use the nozzle diameter as the diameter of the extrusion cross-section. It shouldn't be higher than that to prevent sagging.
 * A second way to compute a bridge flow is to use the current layer height, so it shouldn't protrude below it. Note that may create too thin extrusions and so a bad bridge quality.
 * A Third way to compute a bridge flow is to continue to use the current flow/section (mm3 per mm). If there is no current flow, it will use the solid infill one. To use if you have some difficulties with the big flow changes from infill flow to bridge flow and vice-versa, the bridge flow ratio let you compensate for the change in speed. 
The preview will display the expected shape of the bridge extrusion (cylinder), don't expect a magical thick and solid air to flatten the extrusion magically.

superslicer.filament_custom_variables.label: Custom Filament variables

A value that can be parsed as a int or float will be avaible as a numeric value.
A value that is enclosed by double-quotes will be available as a string (without the quotes)
A value that only takes values as 'true' or 'false' will be a boolean)

superslicer.overhangs_type.label: Overhangs flow baseline

To use if you have some difficulties with the big flow changes from perimeter flow to overhang flow and vice-versa, the overhang flow ratio let you compensate for the change in speed.

superslicer.no_perimeter_unsupported_alg.label: No perimeters on bridge areas
superslicer.no_perimeter_unsupported_alg.tooltip:
Experimental option to remove perimeters where there is nothing under them and where a bridged infill should be better. 
 * Remove perimeters: remove the unsupported perimeters, leave the bridge area as-is.
 * Keep only bridges: remove the perimeters in the bridge areas, keep only bridges that end in solid area.
 * Keep bridges and overhangs: remove the unsupported perimeters, keep only bridges that end in solid area, fill the rest with overhang perimeters+bridges.
 * Fill the voids with bridges: remove the unsupported perimeters, draw bridges over the whole hole.* !! this one can escalate to problems with overhangs shaped like  /\, so you should use it only on one layer at a time via the height-range modifier!
!!Computationally intensive!!.
superslicer.no_perimeter_unsupported_alg.provenance: Ported from SuperSlicer@1f3d287:src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp:4833; GUI: resources/ui_layout/default/print.ui:107 (Perimeters & Shell > Advanced)

superslicer.perimeter_bonding.label: Perimeter bonding
superslicer.perimeter_bonding.tooltip:
This setting may slightly degrade the quality of your external perimeter, in exchange for a better bonding between perimeters.Use it if you have great difficulties with perimeter bonding, for example with high temperature filaments.
This percentage is the % of overlap between perimeters, a bit like perimeter_overlap and external_perimeter_overlap, but in reverse. You have to set perimeter_overlap and external_perimeter_overlap to 100%, or this setting has no effect. 0: no effect, 50%: half of the nozzle will be over an already extruded perimeter while extruding a new one, unless it's an external one).
Note: it needs the external and perimeter overlap to be at 100% and to print the external perimeter first.
superslicer.perimeter_bonding.provenance: Ported from SuperSlicer@1f3d287:src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp:4885; GUI: resources/ui_layout/default/print.ui:129 (Perimeters & Shell > External perimeter first)

superslicer.perimeter_extrusion_spacing.label: Perimeter spacing
superslicer.perimeter_extrusion_spacing.tooltip:
Like Perimeter width but spacing is the distance between two perimeter lines (as they overlap a bit, it's not the same).
You can set either 'Spacing', or 'Width'; the other will be calculated, using the perimeter 'Overlap' percentages and default layer height.
superslicer.perimeter_extrusion_spacing.provenance: Ported from SuperSlicer@1f3d287:src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp:4931; GUI: resources/ui_layout/default/print.ui:471 (Width & Flow > Extrusion width)

superslicer.perimeter_extrusion_change_o.label: Perimeters spacing change on even layers
superslicer.perimeter_extrusion_change_o.tooltip:
Change width on every even layer (and not on odd layers like the first one) for better overlap with adjacent layers and getting stringer shells. Try values about +/- 0.1 with different sign for external and internal perimeters.
This could be combined with extra permeters on even layers.
Works as absolute spacing or a % of the spacing.
set 0 to disable

superslicer.perimeter_direction.label: Perimeter direction
superslicer.perimeter_direction.tooltip: Default direction to print the perimeters (contours and holes): clockwise (CW) or counter-clockwise (CCW).
superslicer.perimeter_direction.provenance: Ported from SuperSlicer@1f3d287:src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp:4960; GUI: resources/ui_layout/default/print.ui:53 (Perimeters & Shell > Quality)

superslicer.perimeter_fan_speed.label: Internal Perimeter fan speed
superslicer.perimeter_fan_speed.tooltip:

superslicer.perimeter_loop.label: Perimeters loop
superslicer.perimeter_loop.tooltip: Join the perimeters to create only one continuous extrusion without any z-hop. Long inside travel (from external to holes) are not extruded to give some space to the infill.
superslicer.perimeter_loop.provenance: Ported from SuperSlicer@1f3d287:src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp:4988; GUI: resources/ui_layout/default/print.ui:109 (Perimeters & Shell > Advanced)

superslicer.perimeter_loop_seam.label: Perimeter loop seam
superslicer.perimeter_loop_seam.provenance: Ported from SuperSlicer@1f3d287:src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp:4997; GUI: resources/ui_layout/default/print.ui:110 (Perimeters & Shell > Advanced)

superslicer.perimeter_overlap.label: Perimeter overlap
superslicer.perimeter_overlap.tooltip:
This setting allows you to reduce the overlap between the perimeters, to reduce the impact of the perimeters' artifacts. 100% means that no gap is left, and 0% means that perimeters are not touching each other anymore.
It's very experimental, please report about the usefulness.

superslicer.perimeter_reverse.label: Perimeter reversal on even layers
superslicer.perimeter_reverse.tooltip: On even layers, all perimeter loops are reversed (it disables the overhang reversal, so it doesn't double-reverse).That setting will likely create defects on the perimeters, so it's only useful is for materials that have some direction-dependent properties (stress lines).

superslicer.perimeter_round_corners.label: Round corners for perimeters
superslicer.perimeter_round_corners.tooltip:
Internal perimeters will go around sharp corners by turning around instead of making the same sharp corner. This can help when there are visible holes in sharp corners on internal perimeters.
Can incur some more processing time, and corners are a bit less sharp.
superslicer.perimeter_round_corners.provenance: Ported from SuperSlicer@1f3d287:src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp:5030; GUI: resources/ui_layout/default/print.ui:112 (Perimeters & Shell > Advanced)

superslicer.perimeters_hole.label: Max perimeter count for holes
superslicer.perimeters_hole.tooltip:
This option sets the number of perimeters to have over holes. Note that if a hole-perimeter fuse with the contour, then it will go around like a contour perimeter.
If disabled, holes will have the same number of perimeters as contour. Cannot be enabled at the same time as Arachne generator.
Note that Slic3r may increase this number automatically when it detects sloping surfaces which benefit from a higher number of perimeters if the Extra Perimeters option is enabled.

superslicer.priming_position.label: Priming position
superslicer.priming_position.tooltip:
Coordinates of the left front corner of the priming patch.
If set to 0,0 then the position is computed automatically.
superslicer.priming_position.provenance: Ported from SuperSlicer@1f3d287:src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp:5103; GUI: resources/ui_layout/default/print.ui:580 (Multiple extruders > Wipe tower)

superslicer.printer_custom_variables.label: Custom Printer variables
superslicer.printer_custom_variables.tooltip:
You can add data accessible to custom-gcode macros.
Each line can define one variable.
The format is 'variable_name=value'. the variable name should only have [a-zA-Z0-9] characters or '_'.
A value that can be parsed as a int or float will be avaible as a numeric value.
A value that is enclosed by double-quotes will be available as a string (without the quotes)
A value that only takes values as 'true' or 'false' will be a boolean)
Every other value will be parsed as a string as-is.
Advice: before using a variable, it's safer to use the function 'default_XXX(variable_name, default_value)' (enclosed in bracket as it's a script) in case it's not set. You can replace XXX by 'int' 'bool' 'double' 'string'.

superslicer.fan_printer_min_speed.label: Minimum fan speed
superslicer.fan_printer_min_speed.tooltip: This setting represents the minimum fan speed (like minimum PWM) your fan needs to work.

superslicer.print_bed_temperature.label: Bed Temperature
superslicer.print_bed_temperature.tooltip:
Override the temperature of the bed.
If disabled, uses the highest bed temperature from all filaments used in the first layer.
superslicer.print_bed_temperature.provenance: Ported from SuperSlicer@1f3d287:src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp:5144; GUI: resources/ui_layout/default/print.ui:585 (Multiple extruders > Advanced)

superslicer.print_first_layer_bed_temper.label: First Layer Bed Temperature
superslicer.print_first_layer_bed_temper.tooltip:
Override the temperature of the bed while printing the first layer.
If disabled, uses the highest first layer bed temperature from all filaments used in the first layer.
Set to 0 to prevent the slicer to do any first layer bed command.

superslicer.print_first_layer_temperatur.label: First Layer Temperature
superslicer.print_first_layer_temperatur.tooltip: Override the temperature of the extruder (for the first layer). Avoid making too many changes, it won't stop for cooling/heating.May only work on Height range modifiers.

superslicer.print_retract_length.label: Retraction length
superslicer.print_retract_length.tooltip: Override the retract_length setting from the printer config. Used for calibration.

superslicer.print_retract_lift.label: Z-lift override
superslicer.print_retract_lift.tooltip: Set the new lift-z value for this override. 0 will disable the z-lift. -& to disable. May only work on Height range modifiers.

superslicer.print_temperature.label: Temperature
superslicer.print_temperature.tooltip: Override the temperature of the extruder. Avoid making too many changes, it won't stop for cooling/heating. May only work on Height range modifiers.

superslicer.print_settings_modified.label: Print settings modified

superslicer.raft_contact_distance_type.label: Raft contact distance type
superslicer.raft_contact_distance_type.tooltip:
How to compute the vertical z-distance.
From filament: it uses the nearest bit of the filament. When a bridge is extruded, it goes below the current plane.
From plane: it uses the plane-z. Same as 'from filament' if no 'bridge' is extruded.
None: No z-offset. Useful for Soluble supports.

superslicer.raft_layer_height.label: Raft layer height
superslicer.raft_layer_height.tooltip:
Maximum layer height for the raft, after the first layer that uses the first layer height, and before the interface layers.
Can be a % of the nozzle diameter
If set to 0, the support layer height will be used.

superslicer.raft_interface_layer_height.tooltip:

superslicer.region_gcode.label: Per region G-code
superslicer.region_gcode.tooltip:
This code is inserted when a region is starting to print something (infill, perimeter, ironing). It's main advantage is when you use it as a object modifer(right click on a model to add it there)
Special variables: 'layer_num','layer_z'

superslicer.gcode_command_buffer.label: Command buffer
superslicer.gcode_command_buffer.tooltip: Buffer the firmware has for gcode comamnds. Allow to have some burst of command with a rate over 'max_gcode_per_second' for a few instant.

superslicer.gcode_min_length.label: Minimum extrusion length
superslicer.gcode_min_length.tooltip:
When outputting gcode, this setting ensure that there is almost no commands more than this value apart. Be sure to also use max_gcode_per_second instead, as it's much better when you have very different speeds for features (Too many too small commands may overload the firmware / connection).
Disabled if set to 0.

superslicer.gcode_min_resolution.label: minimum resolution
superslicer.gcode_min_resolution.tooltip:
Maximum deviation of exported G-code paths from their full resolution counterparts when some commands are culled by 'gcode_min_length' or 'max_gcode_per_second' to not overload the firmware.
Can be a % of perimeter width.

superslicer.resolution_internal.label: Internal resolution
superslicer.resolution_internal.tooltip:
Minimum detail resolution, used for internal structures (gapfill and some infill patterns).
Don't put a too-small value, as it may create too many very small segments that may be difficult to display and print if your main resolution parameter is also very small.

superslicer.retract_lift_before_travel.label: Minimum travel after z lift
superslicer.retract_lift_before_travel.tooltip: Z lift is not triggered when travel moves are shorter than this length.

superslicer.retract_lift_first_layer.label: Enforce lift on first layer
superslicer.retract_lift_first_layer.tooltip:
Select this option to enforce z-lift on the first layer.
Useful to still use the lift on the first layer even if the 'Only lift Z below' (retract_lift_above) is higher than 0.

superslicer.retract_lift_top.label: Lift only on
superslicer.retract_lift_top.tooltip: Select this option to not use/enforce the z-lift on a top surface.

superslicer.seam_angle_cost.label: Seam angle cost
superslicer.seam_angle_cost.tooltip:
Cost of placing the seam at a bad angle. The worst angle (max penalty) is when it's flat.
100% is the default penalty
superslicer.seam_angle_cost.provenance: Ported from SuperSlicer@1f3d287:src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp:5673; GUI: resources/ui_layout/default/print.ui:79 (Perimeters & Shell > Seam)

superslicer.seam_gap_external.label: Seam gap for external perimeters
superslicer.seam_gap_external.tooltip:
To avoid visible seam, the extrusion can be stoppped a bit before the end of the loop.
 this setting is enforced only for external perimeter. It overrides 'seam_gap' if different than 0
Can be a mm or a % of the current seam gap.

superslicer.seam_notch_all.label: Seam notch
superslicer.seam_notch_all.tooltip:
It's sometimes very problematic to have a little buldge from the seam. This setting move the seam inside the part, in a little cavity (for every seams in external perimeters, unless it's in an overhang).
The size of the cavity is in mm or a % of the external perimeter width. It's overriden by the two other 'seam notch' setting when applicable.
Set zero to disable.

superslicer.seam_notch_angle.label: Seam notch maximum angle
superslicer.seam_notch_angle.tooltip:
If the (external) angle at the seam is higher than this value, then no notch will be set. If the angle is too high, there isn't enough room for the notch.
Can't be lower than 180° or it filters everything. At 360, it allows everything.

superslicer.seam_notch_inner.label: Seam notch for round holes
superslicer.seam_notch_inner.tooltip:
In convex holes (circular/oval), it's sometimes very problematic to have a little buldge from the seam. This setting move the seam inside the part, in a little cavity (for all external perimeters in convex holes, unless it's in an overhang).

superslicer.seam_notch_outer.label: Seam notch for round perimeters
superslicer.seam_notch_outer.tooltip:

superslicer.seam_travel_cost.label: Seam travel cost

superslicer.seam_visibility.label: Seam visibility check

superslicer.slice_merge_dent.label: Slice mmu merge: dent
superslicer.slice_merge_dent.tooltip:

superslicer.slice_merge_min_width.label: Slice mmu merge: min width

superslicer.small_perimeter_max_length.label: Max small perimeters length
superslicer.small_perimeter_max_length.tooltip:

Can be a mm or a % of the nozzle diameter.

superslicer.solid_infill_below_layer_are.label: Solid infill layer threshold area
superslicer.solid_infill_below_layer_are.tooltip: Force solid infill for the whole layer when the combined area of all objects that are printed at the same layer is smaller than this value.

superslicer.solid_infill_below_width.label: Solid infill threshold width
superslicer.solid_infill_below_width.tooltip:

Can be a % of the current solid infill spacing.

superslicer.solid_infill_overlap.label: Solid infill overlap

This setting allows you to reduce the overlap between the lines of the solid fill, to reduce the % filled if you see overextrusion signs on solid areas. superslicer.solid_infill_extrusion_spaci.label: Solid infill spacing

superslicer.start_gcode_manual.label: Only custom Start G-code
superslicer.start_gcode_manual.tooltip:

If set to true, you have to write a good and complete start_gcode, as no checks are made anymore.
Exemple:
G21 ; set units to millimeters
G90 ; use absolute coordinates
{if use_relative_e_distances}M83{else}M82{endif}
G92 E0 ; reset extrusion distance

superslicer.solid_over_perimeters.label: No solid infill over perimeters
superslicer.solid_over_perimeters.tooltip:

By setting this to something higher than 0, you can control this behaviour, which might be desirable if 
undesirable solid infill is being generated on slopes.
The number set here indicates the number of layers between the inside of the part and the air at and beyond which solid infill should no longer be added above/below. superslicer.support_material_acceleratio.label: Support acceleration
superslicer.support_material_acceleratio.tooltip:
This is the acceleration your printer will use for support material.
